newsitem.title: CONGO: S.Africa blames Kabila for Zaire talks delay.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa blames Kabila for Zaire talks delay.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila has forced postponement of talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko by raising new security concerns, the South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Wednesday.
"We are still continuing discussions.... I think we can predict it (the meeting) will start tomorrow," he told reporters waiting for the meeting, due to be chaired by President Nelson Mandela.
Mobutu arrived in Pointe Noire earlier on Wednesday
Pahad, who has played a central role in South African efforts to bring the Zairean leaders together for a second time, appeared irritated about Kabila's last-minute delay.

He said South African Defence Minister Joe Modise had flown by helicopter to Soyo in Angola to fetch Kabila, but had learned later that the rebel leader had landed in Cabinda, an Angolan enclave between Zaire and Congo..
"We cannot believe it is a stalling tactic. We have to find out what it is about. I can only reflect to you what we were told officially," he said.

Pahad said Mandela, waiting in Pointe Noire with Congolese President Pascal Lissouba, had been in contact with other African leaders as well as the United States and Britain in a bid to bolster the peace process.
